items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: if you joined during the era that Fletcher's band, usually Earl and Buster Bailey and Red Allen and Coleman Hawkins

ctx.x: -- and he did play it, yeah.

Because when it first came out, I remember Hawk's reaction about this thing, and he said, 'Well, this is what I'm going to have to get with, you know, and he did, and, man, he could play it. But I still contend that you've got to know your instrument, and you've got to know the chord, something about it. You just don't play this by ear. Now you never did catch Red Allen, guys like that playing bebop. See? Gail Brockman was another guy, trumpet player, that, he played a little, but the fundamentals, man, you had…

And so I just decided to pass it up and not go that route. But I enjoy listening to it; even today I do, especially when the guys play it and it makes sense. I don't mean these little, young -- because I had this little trumpet player, Benny Harris, and he made some one nighters with me, and he played that stuff, man. And he would come behind that bebop and start swinging. And then he'd go back into the bebop, and he was versatile (inaudible), you know. That little cat could play, man! So I have nothing against…

items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: Henry Red Allen, incidentally, was in on this session too... I had met some great guys that played great solos in there like Henry "Red" Allen

ctx.x: Sometimes you were out for two or three years, you didn't see your family. You didn't have any, in fact, you were served papers, you know, one of those things. They had a saying once, join John Fletcher Henderson's band, see the world and be a bachelor, you know. So this is what actually happened. But he paid them -- like you would have 31 one nighters, you would get a nightly salary, you know, which was far more equivalent according to working, you know, week stands, where you got, you know, a flat salary for a…

He'd have one or two in the band that would be home boys. They would miss their families, you know, and this is where you would have to inject quite a bit of humor or comedy to keep the guy from being so lonesome, like Henry Red Allen, you know.
